texts: When the book was written, none of these was an FDA-approved indication for percutaneous PFO closure: E, none of the above.
Occluders had been used off label; earlier humanitarian approvals had been withdrawn, and the first randomized trials had not shown a clear benefit.
This has changed: in October 2016 the FDA approved the Amplatzer PFO Occluder, and in 2018 the Gore Cardioform, after the RESPECT, CLOSE and REDUCE trials.

The approved use is to reduce recurrent ischaemic stroke in patients, mostly aged 18 to 60, whose stroke is cryptogenic and thought to come from paradoxical embolism; today A would be the closest answer.
A shunt ratio (Qp/Qs) above 1.5:1 is a reason to close an atrial septal defect, not a PFO.
In the picture, the clerk stamps none of the requests, until the messenger's news brings the stamp toward the lightning from a clear sky.
Memory hook: in the book no stamp; since late 2016, the stamp for the lightning from a clear sky.
